algorithm.Title: Warts - Male (Adult)
algorithm.ContentSet: IST Open-Source Guideline Content | Adult | Male
Definition: Assessment of a suspected wart or verruca in children and adults, with safeguards for uncertain diagnosis, genital lesions, pregnancy, diabetes, poor circulation, and immunocompromise.

questions.Question: Is this an open traumatic skin wound rather than a wart or verruca?
questions.Information: An open traumatic wound belongs in the Skin Injury pathway.

questions.Question: Is the lesion on the face or genitals, changing, bleeding, ulcerated, large, painful, recurrent, or uncertain to be a wart; or does the patient have diabetes, poor circulation, immune suppression, pregnancy, or a genital lesion requiring age-appropriate safeguarding assessment?
questions.Information: These features require diagnosis and treatment selection by a clinician. Genital lesions need confidential, age-appropriate sexual-health and safeguarding assessment; the exact Qatar route is governance-required.

questions.Question: Is this a typical small wart or verruca on intact non-facial, non-genital skin in an otherwise healthy, non-pregnant patient, with none of the features above?
questions.Information: NHS.UK guidance describes typical warts/verrucas as manageable with pharmacy over-the-counter treatments.

advice.Title: Lesion requiring in-person assessment
Content: Use the Qatar governance-approved primary-care, dermatology, sexual-health, or safeguarding pathway. Do not label an uncertain, changing, bleeding, facial, or genital lesion as a wart by telephone. Provide privacy for adolescents when safe and follow local consent and safeguarding policy.
Call Back If: rapid change, persistent bleeding, ulceration, spreading infection, or severe pain.

advice.Title: Low-risk wart care
Content: Do not cut, burn, pick, or share treatment devices. Ask a pharmacist to confirm an age-appropriate product and follow its label; never use wart acids on the face, genitals, broken skin, or without professional advice in pregnancy, diabetes, poor circulation, or immune suppression. Wash hands after contact and avoid sharing towels, socks, or shoes.
Call Back If: growth, colour or shape change, bleeding, ulceration, pain, or diagnostic uncertainty; skin infection or failure to improve.

references: NHS.UK, "Warts and verrucas", https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/warts-and-verrucas/ (page last reviewed 25 July 2023)
